verdict: Mostly boilerplate course content with embedded tactical prompts. Real gold concentrated in segments 15-20 (Trigify social listening + SuperSearch filtering).
portion_doctrine: This document is 80% course wrapper + prompt library, 20% tactical substance. Segments 11-14 are primarily onboarding/project setup theory. Segments 15-20 contain signal-driven prospecting methodology (social listening via Trigify, SuperSearch filtering, evergreen campaigns). Strip all nav/UI/course scaffolding; extract only the operating methods, filter architecture, signal categories, and reply rate benchmarks.
operating_rules: Strategy before automation: AI cannot fix weak offers, fuzzy ICP, or messy data.
Quality over quantity: Smaller lists of well-targeted prospects outperform larger lists of poorly-targeted ones. Avoid the volume trap.
Signal-driven outreach beats static lists: Reach people whose recent behavior suggests genuine interest, not random prospects.
Individual timing matters more than company timing: Company signals (funding, hiring) show qualification; social signals show individual receptivity right now.
Evergreen campaigns beat batch campaigns: Event-triggered outreach maintains high conversion; static list exhaustion produces inconsistent results.
Keep the stack lean: Lead finder, enrichment, outreach, scoring, simple nurture only. Eliminate tool-hopping.
Explicit trigger commands for skills: Each skill needs a unique command ([cold-copywriting], etc.) to prevent Claude from selecting wrong tool.
Monitor three profile segments: Own brand engagement (warmest), competitor engagement (qualified but requires soft messaging), thought leader engagement (interested audience).
Avoid surveillance creepiness: Lead with topic value, not tracking behavior. Don't say 'I noticed you engaged with X'; say 'Companies in your space are seeing Y results.'
Test and iterate on searches: No search is perfect first try. Track which leads respond, refine criteria based on patterns.

components: ICP definition: industries, sizes, roles, key triggers
Right lead definition: matching ICP, has problem you solve, can make decisions

categories.name: Own Brand
categories.action: Monitor LinkedIn profile engagement (all posts); reach out to people liking/commenting; these are warm leads with demonstrated awareness
categories.setup: Use Trigify to pull engagement data; push to Instantly via integration

categories.name: Competitors
categories.action: Monitor C-suite/founders at competitor companies (not brand page, personal profiles - higher engagement volume). Reach out on topic, not surveillance.
categories.caveat: Don't say 'I saw you engaged with [competitor]'; say 'Companies adopting [competitor's approach] are seeing [outcomes]'
categories.setup: Identify best competitor to monitor, pull founder/CTO profiles, track engagement

categories.name: Thought Leaders
categories.action: Monitor prominent voices in your space (practitioners, founders at complementary tools, industry analysts). Audience of engaged followers = prospect pool.
categories.messaging: Mention thought leader in postscript as recommendation (mutual alignment, not creepy)
categories.setup: Map thought leader content your ICP engages with; track their audience engagement

specific_tactics: Skip already owned toggle: Prevent duplicate enrichment/contact in SuperSearch
Job title filtering: Use 'contains' (manager but not project manager) rather than exact match; layer in management level + department
Employee range: 100-1000 is sweet spot mentioned in example; can combine with revenue filters (10-50M)
News filter: Most powerful trigger; identifies companies with events (office closure, expansion, funding, CMO promoted to CEO, acquisition, product launch, new campaign)
One lead per company toggle: Reach single decision-maker per org instead of multiple marketers
Lookalike domain cloning: Drop best customer domain into filter; SuperSearch finds similar companies
Post-signal routing: Add qualification AI step before campaign entry to verify engagement is relevant (not false positive)
Thought leader mention in postscript: 'Check out [thought leader] on [topic]' creates mutual alignment without surveillance feel
Combine three signal types: Recently funded + hiring for marketing + using HubSpot = high-intent list
Use frameworks uploaded to Sales Brain files: Don't write from scratch each email; reference company framework (e.g., AIDA, Problem-Agitate-Solve)
prompts: Claude Skills explicit trigger command pattern: [cold-copywriting] or [email-sequence] to force skill selection
ICP definition prompt for Sales Brain: 'Define the industries, sizes, roles, and key triggers that make someone a strong fit'
Evergreen campaign setup: 'Configure system to reach out whenever someone matches criteria AND triggers relevant signal (vs. static list load)'
Thought leader recommendation postscript: 'Check out [name] on [topic] worth diving into' (not surveillance, value-driven)
Copy framework for signal-driven outreach: 'Lead with metrics/outcomes from leading companies in their space, not monitoring behavior'
SuperSearch filters example: 'Mid-senior marketing professionals, US, 100-1000 employees, recently launched new product'
Competitor monitoring angle: 'Focus on the topic competitor discusses, not the competitor itself' (creates relevance without creepiness)

gates: ICP clarity gate: Define industries, sizes, roles, triggers before prospecting. Fuzzy ICP fails regardless of AI.
Signal relevance gate: Add AI qualification step to evergreen campaigns before entry to filter false positives.
List quality gate: Test first 50 leads from search manually. If irrelevant, refine filters before scaling.
Delivery health gate: Monitor domain warmup, inbox placement, response patterns. Stop if unsubscribe rate or complaint rate spikes.
Reply context gate: AI Reply Agent should verify thread context before auto-responding; manual review flag for unusual threads.

contradictions: Course emphasizes 'quality over quantity' but includes massive Supersearch prompt library (100+ permutations), creating impression that volume of tools matters
Sales Brain architecture requires significant Claude Project setup time, but evergreen campaigns (Trigify + Instantly direct) skip this entirely; positioning is unclear on when each is worth the lift
Thought leader engagement as warm signal, but messaging guidance explicitly says DON'T mention the specific thought leader (creates friction vs. warm positioning)
weird_gold: Trigify + Instantly users report 20-25% positive reply rates, which is extraordinarily high. Document doesn't explain if this is opens, replies, or qualified replies. Benchmark feels optimized/survivorship bias (featured case studies).
SuperSearch 'news filter' is positioned as most powerful but least explained (vague reference to 'entire Internet scraping'). No clarity on data freshness, false positive rate, or cost.
Claude Projects + Instantly MCP integration is positioned as future of outbound, but document is written as course for Instantly standalone users; integration feels experimental/not yet mainstream
Evergreen campaigns by definition never exhaust their list (continuous new entries), yet document shows no guidance on managing campaign fatigue or audience overlap over time
'One lead per company' toggle in SuperSearch is unexplained in context: Is this one lead per outreach motion or global? If global, how do you handle expansion/multi-touch?
